question: Why does the same punishing downhill run leave far less soreness when repeated a few weeks later?
answer: The first bout protects against the next. Known as the repeated-bout effect, it appears after a single session and lasts for weeks. Nerves recruit the muscle differently, connective tissue stiffens and the inflammatory response is damped. The second descent does less damage, not merely hurts less.
move: The first hard dose of anything teaches the body what to expect.
ask: What hard thing did I handle better the second time because the first dose taught my body?
source: McHugh, Scand J Med Sci Sports, 2003
reference: McHugh, Recent advances in the understanding of the repeated bout effect, Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports, 2003
